# Wild Pokémon: Pokémon Adamant Diamond

Every area with wild Pokémon, as this game has them. The tables are Diamond's own, with the same levels and the same odds per slot.

- **Grass and cave floor**: the Chance columns add up every slot of the same Pokémon. The time on your DS clock picks the column when you enter the area. When all three are the same there's one column.
- **Hours**, by season: spring 5:00-9:59 morning, 10:00-19:59 day, 20:00-4:59 night; summer 4:00-8:59 morning, 9:00-20:59 day, 21:00-3:59 night; autumn 6:00-9:59 morning, 10:00-19:59 day, 20:00-5:59 night; winter 7:00-10:59 morning, 11:00-18:59 day, 19:00-6:59 night. With seasons off (see [options](options.md)) it's always spring's hours.
- **Old, Good and Super Rod** each fish their own table. Each rod bites as often as in the original games.
- **Swarm**: swarms start after the Hall of Fame, with the National Pokédex, when you talk to Dawn's or Lucas's little sibling at their home in Sandgem Town. After that, talk to them to hear today's swarm. On that area's two 20% grass slots the swarm's Pokémon appear, at those slots' levels, until midnight. It changes daily.
- There is no Poké Radar and no Pokémon appears from a Game Boy Advance game in slot 2, so those lists of the original games aren't here.
- **After the Hall of Fame**, each slot where the two versions' tables differ brings Lustrous Pearl's Pokémon half of the time. Stantler, Smeargle, Swellow and Loudred, which only the Poké Radar found, come the same way in the slots the Radar used. Each area's "after the Hall of Fame" table lists them, with the Pokémon they share the slot with. On the day of an area's swarm, the swarm keeps its two slots.

[Honey trees](#honey-trees), [the Great Marsh's daily Pokémon](#great-marsh-daily-pokémon), [the Trophy Garden](#trophy-garden-daily-pokémon), [Feebas](#feebas) and [the Grand Underground's Hideaways](#grand-underground-hideaways) are at the end. One-time Pokémon are on the [post-game page](postgame-diamond.md).

## Honey trees

21 trees, one each in: Eterna Forest (outside), Floaroma Meadow, Fuego Ironworks (outside), Route 205 North, Route 205 South, Route 206, Route 207, Route 208, Route 209, Route 210 North, Route 210 South, Route 211 East, Route 212 North, Route 212 South, Route 213, Route 214, Route 215, Route 218, Route 221, Route 222, Valley Windworks.

Slather Honey on a tree (a man in Floaroma Meadow sells it for $100), and come back after 6 hours and within a day. 10% of the time nothing comes; otherwise the Pokémon is level 5-15. Four of the trees (they depend on your Trainer ID) can also bring Munchlax: on those, Group B is the common one and Group C is 1%. On any other tree Group A is 70% and Group B 20%. Slathering the same tree twice in a row keeps the same group 90% of the time.

| Slot | Chance | Group A | Group B | Group C |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 40% | Wurmple | Combee | Munchlax |
| 2 | 20% | Silcoon | Burmy | Munchlax |
| 3 | 20% | Combee | Cherubi | Munchlax |
| 4 | 10% | Burmy | Aipom | Munchlax |
| 5 | 5% | Cherubi | Heracross | Munchlax |
| 6 | 5% | Aipom | Wurmple | Munchlax |

## Great Marsh daily Pokémon

Each of the six areas draws today's Pokémon from one list, for the two 5% slots of its grass. The lists:

- **Before the Hall of Fame:** Azurill, Bibarel, Bidoof, Carnivine, Croagunk, Golduck, Marill, Quagsire, Roselia, Skorupi, Staravia, Wooper.
- **After the Hall of Fame (National Pokédex):** Carnivine, Croagunk, Drapion, Exeggcute, Golduck, Gulpin, Kangaskhan, Paras, Roselia, Shroomish, Skorupi, Staravia, Toxicroak, Yanma.

## Trophy Garden daily Pokémon

Talk to Mr. Backlot in the Pokémon Mansion on Route 212: with the National Pokédex he names a Pokémon he's seen in his garden, and it joins the Trophy Garden's two 5% grass slots: Eevee, Bonsly, Happiny, Meowth, Cleffa, Clefairy, Igglybuff, Plusle, Jigglypuff, Porygon, Castform, Minun, Mime Jr., Marill, Chansey, Azurill.

## Feebas

Mt. Coronet B1F's lake: four of its 528 water tiles hold Feebas today, different each day. Fishing on one of them with any rod, half of the bites are a Feebas (level 10-20); the others come from the rod's own table.

## Grand Underground Hideaways

Pokémon walk around in the Hideaways: touch one for a battle. A new set appears each time you enter. More kinds appear as you go on, and everyone's level follows your badges:

| Badges | Level |
|---|---|
| 0-1 | 16-20 |
| 2 | 25-29 |
| 3 | 29-33 |
| 4 | 33-37 |
| 5 | 36-40 |
| 6 | 39-43 |
| 7 | 42-46 |
| 8 | 50-55 |
| Champion | 58-63 |

On half of your visits one of the Pokémon is the Hideaway's rare one. All kinds are equally common. From Champion on, Lustrous Pearl's Pokémon of each Hideaway come too (the Champion rows). See [the Underground page](underground.md) for how to get there.

## Hidden Grottos

In each Hideaway, a narrow path in a wall. Level 25-29, with the Pokémon's Hidden Ability. Each grotto refills when empty; the percentages are how often a refill is that kind of slot. The items are on [the Underground page](underground.md).
